summary: Async embedding commit offset causing missing top-k candidates and rerank P95 spike
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent missing top-k results from the reranking endpoint for a subset of queries after a bulk embedding ingest. Impact: missing candidates and long tail latency (p95 for rerank requests increased from 120ms to 1.8s for affected calls).

Impact:
- Clipper Analytics (dedicated tenant) observed a 4% drop in returned candidate counts for /rerank and a correlated p95 latency spike in us-east between 2026-03-11T22:05 and 2026-03-12T03:30 UTC.
- User-visible symptom: search results show fewer items and occasional empty candidate sets for queries that previously returned results.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment in prod-us-east (private overlay).
- Embedding ingest pipeline writes embeddings to object store and then emits an "ingest-commit" marker via the ingest-proxy.
- Reranker uses approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) shards with async refresh when new commits are announced.

Steps to reproduce (from customer reproduction recipe):
1) Perform large embedding backfill (approx 1.2M vectors) into customer's namespace with the ingest tool (batch size 1024, async_commit=true).
2) Immediately run a set of production queries that previously returned stable top-10 candidates.
3) Observe returned candidate counts and latency via the client logs and Redwood Console traces.

Observed behavior:
- Some queries return fewer than expected candidates (0-7 instead of 10) and occasionally return an empty candidate set.
- Rerank p95 latency for affected queries jumps to ~1.8s while p50 remains ~120ms.
- Console traces show rerank service waiting on follower-refresh timeouts and then falling back to a smaller shard set.

Expected behavior:
- After ingest commit, reranker should include new vectors deterministically. Request latency should not spike for stable queries and candidate count should remain stable.

Relevant logs & traces:
- Ingest-proxy logs show commit announcements published at 2026-03-11T22:07:18Z and 2026-03-12T01:44:03Z.
- Reranker traces show a sequence: ANN_SHARD_REFRESH_WAIT -> ANN_PARTIAL_FALLBACK -> RESPOND_WITH_SMALLEST_SET.
- Proxy->reranker handoff occasionally includes a commit_offset that is 1 behind the actual object-store commit timestamp (see ingest-proxy trace id ip-2721-commit-0x7f9).

Attachments: customer-provided curl logs, Console p95 charts, sample query IDs and timestamps.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:12 - Support (Maya Patel): Initial triage completed with customer. Collected curl logs, sample query IDs, and timeline. Escalated to infra on-call.

2026-03-12 11:04 - Infra (Jared Collins): Reproduced locally with a small backfill using async_commit. Observed a commit-announce race where the reranker sometimes sees an announce for batch N before all segment metadata for N is available on the follower. Opened hypothesis H1.

2026-03-12 13:27 - Customer (Clipper Analytics SRE - Theo Ramos): Noted that manual refresh (POST /admin/ann/refresh) temporarily restores full results. Provided additional timestamps where empty sets occurred.

2026-03-13 08:55 - Engineering (Lina Chen): Investigating proxy code path. Found that transient gzip compression on the proxy side occasionally truncates the trailing metadata record when commit announcements are piggybacked with batch heartbeats. Working on a repro with compression toggled off.

2026-03-14 10:30 - Jared Collins: Added temporary guard in reranker to wait for segment-metadata TTL (200ms) before honoring an announce. This reduced reproductions in staging but needs a durable fix; plan to push a controlled patch and measure impact on latency.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis H1: Race between ingest commit announcement and final segment metadata write causes reranker to refresh using incomplete shard metadata -> missing vectors.
Hypothesis H2: Compression/truncation in proxy can chop off trailing commit_offset bytes when announcements are coalesced with heartbeats, leading to offset mismatch.

Evidence: Multiple traces show reranker received announce at T but subsequent segment metadata lookup returned 404 for ~120-350ms window. The ingest-proxy log for ip-2721 shows a mismatch between commit_id and object-store HEAD at the same time.
Staging repro: With N=50k vectors and async_commit enabled, disabling proxy gzip eliminated the repro for 10/10 runs. Re-enabling gzip reintroduced the issue in 3/10 runs.
Temporary mitigation: Added 200ms guarded wait in reranker (staging) before accepting announcements. This reduced empty-set rate from 4%->0.3% in duplicates of the customer's workload.

Potential root cause: ingest-proxy coalesces multiple control messages into a single payload to reduce network overhead. When the payload crosses a compression block boundary, the trailing control record (commit_offset) can be truncated on some proxy builds due to a buffer-edge bug introduced in proxy v2.14.6.
Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-proxy/pull/789 (buffer-edge fix) currently in review. Monitoring results from a canary build show removal of truncation repros.
Impact tradeoff: Guarded wait adds a small delay for fresh-announce visibility (~200ms) but reduces customer-visible missing candidates. Need evaluation against latency SLOs for the dedicated plan.
resolution: In progress: Patch for ingest-proxy buffer handling merged into PR 789; canary deploy scheduled for 2026-03-15 in prod-us-east with feature flag off by default. Temporary reranker guard wait will be rolled back after ingest-proxy fix validated. Postmortem to include code-level test for compressed control-message coalescing and an automated canary that exercises async_commit flows.
resolution_notes: Plan: 1) Deploy ingest-proxy fix as canary to 10% of customer's hosts. 2) Monitor Console metrics for empty candidate rate and rerank p95. 3) If stable after 24h, roll out to full cluster and remove temporary guarded wait in reranker. 4) Create regression test in CI that reproduces coalesced compressed control messages.
Follow-ups: update ingest-runbook to include a validation step after large backfills; inform customer SRE when full rollout scheduled.
